lead: Every physical security key and smart card this realm has recorded. A token is recorded only from its own attestation: today a security key registered with enterprise attestation, whose certificate names its serial. A serial typed by anybody is never recorded. Each token lists the passkeys and certificates on it and who registered them.
capped: This list is the newest thousand tokens. Search by serial or person for any other.
none: No hardware token is recorded in this realm.
lostWhat: Reporting a token lost marks it lost at once, then removes each passkey on it, revokes each certificate on it for key compromise, sends a CAEP credential-change for each and ends the sessions they signed in. A credential that could not be retired is named in the answer and on the audit row, and is still live.
oath.heading: OATH tokens
oath.none: No OATH token is in this realm's inventory.
oath.importLead: The file a token vendor sends with pre-programmed HOTP or TOTP tokens (RFC 6030). Give its pre-shared key, in hexadecimal or base64, or its password. Neither is ever stored. Each key becomes an unassigned token, kept by its serial.
oath.file: The file (paste it, or load it)
oath.what: An unassigned token can be assigned here, or claimed by the person it was handed to: on their portal they type its serial and a code it shows. Its codes then earn the hardware claim hwk while the token is in use. Report the hardware token lost on the first tab to retire it.
